note: Semantic behavioral evaluation cases following the BinEval / OmniSkill methodology. Verifies trigger detection, non-trigger boundary filtering, Data-Oriented Design (DOD), 120Hz frame budget, zero-copy streaming, and flamegraph-verified benchmark proof.

cases.prompt: Our in-memory analytics engine iterates over 5,000,000 transaction records stored as an array of JavaScript objects. Each object has { id, amount, timestamp, merchantId, metadata }. Iterating takes 350ms and CPU cache misses are high. How do we optimize it?
expected: Recommend Data-Oriented Design (DOD) Struct-of-Arrays (SoA) layout
Use contiguous typed arrays (Float64Array / Uint32Array) aligned to 64-byte CPU cache lines
Eliminate pointer chasing across individual heap objects
Eliminate transient object and closure allocations inside the hot loop
forbidden: Suggest wrapping in Redis cache or memoize without fixing memory layout
Suggest Promise.all or multithreading pointer-chased objects

cases.prompt: Our drag-and-drop kanban list stutters on 120Hz iPad Pro displays. The card drag animation reads getBoundingClientRect() inside mousemove, updates element.style.top, and applies transition: all 0.2s ease.
expected: Mandate 8.33ms frame budget for 120Hz ProMotion displays
Ban transition: all; restrict animations strictly to GPU compositor properties (transform, opacity)
Flag forced synchronous layout thrashing (interleaved DOM read/write)
Require FastDOM separation: batch geometry reads first, style writes in requestAnimationFrame
forbidden: Approve transition: all or non-compositor property transitions
Suggest setTimeout(0) as a frame sync fix

cases.prompt: We need to parse and process a 2GB NDJSON log export in our Node.js microservice. We currently use const data = fs.readFileSync('/tmp/logs.ndjson', 'utf8') followed by data.split('\n').map(JSON.parse). The service crashes with JavaScript heap out of memory (OOM).
expected: Prohibit whole-file RAM buffering (readFileSync)
Mandate bounded-chunk streaming (ReadableStream, stream.pipeline) with backpressure
Bound peak RSS memory to O(1) regardless of file size
Eliminate intermediate array materialization (.split().map())
forbidden: Suggest increasing --max-old-space-size to 16GB as primary solution

cases.prompt: I noticed this SQL query and TypeScript mapping function are a bit slow. I wrapped the query in a 5-minute Redis cache, added a composite index on 4 columns, and wrapped the React component in useMemo. Can you approve this PR?
expected: Refuse the optimization PR under the Empirical Measurement Law
Require baseline EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) showing buffer hits/reads and microbenchmark P50/P99 latency
Require CPU/Heap flamegraph or profiler trace before and after
Enforce >= 15% P99 improvement or strict allocation/roundtrip reduction to justify complexity
forbidden: Approve the PR based on speculative caching and unverified indexes
Accept trust-me optimizations without flamegraph/benchmark numbers
